accepted_units.title: From single large values to simultaneous large values and fourth moments
accepted_units.why_material: The source explains that mean-value bounds can be surpassed in the high-real-part region by Halasz-Montgomery, that Huxley's reflection argument reframes the task as simultaneous largeness of two Dirichlet polynomials, and that this paper's variant inserts mean fourth-power information on the critical line.
accepted_units.context_note: The polynomial itself is introduced immediately afterward at lines 30-45; exact displayed notation at lines 19-20 is not needed for this prose-supported strategic move.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual move is notation-robust, but the OCR-damaged display (1.1) requires scan verification before coefficient-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Three character ensembles for one large-value counting problem
accepted_units.why_material: The paper packages the task as counting separated pairs where a variable-character Dirichlet polynomial is large, then distinguishes fixed modulus, primitive conductors bounded by Q, and the principal-character case. This separates one mechanism by the arithmetic ensemble over which it must be controlled.
accepted_units.context_note: Read with the motivation at lines 11-29; the exact theorem bounds at lines 51-58 are quarantined rather than reconstructed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the distinctions among character, modulus, and conductor; the display defining G and the exact separation symbols are OCR-unsafe and need the scan for formal use.

accepted_units.title: Complementary large-value bounds dominate in different density regions
accepted_units.why_material: The author explicitly says the new estimate and Huxley's estimate do not contain one another: the new estimate is roughly sharper for larger V and yields new density information near 4/5, whereas Huxley's is better near 3/4. The density hypothesis and prior threshold results are used as a common comparison target.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the recoverable interpretation of the formula-heavy theorem and corollary at lines 51-96, not a substitute for their exact exponents.

accepted_units.why_material: The paper states the division of labor explicitly: a generalized basic lemma, an elementary inequality that makes the later input usable, and mean-value estimates for partial sums of L-series. This is a compact reusable map of the proof rather than a list of lemma names.

accepted_units.title: Contour shifting converts the large-value object into critical-line partial sums plus error
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 1 and its proof start from an integral identity, shift contours, account for a possible residue, apply the functional equation, split the transformed L-series into a finite partial sum and a remainder, and move the two resulting integrals to different lines so that one supplies the main term and the other an error. The imprimitive case is handled by passing to a primitive character and paying extra local factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof prose at lines 176-201 securely supports the transformation; the OCR-corrupt statement and display (2.1) are retained only as local setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly dependent on contour, functional-equation, and character notation; exact contour locations, truncation lengths, powers, and factors require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line fourth moments control partial sums in long and short regimes
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 3 treats fixed-modulus and bounded-conductor character families. Its proof uses a direct critical-line L-value approximation in one length regime and an integral representation in the other, applying discrete analogues of fourth-moment estimates in both; it also records an alternative proof route that avoids approximate-functional-equation difficulties.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose at lines 272-317 supports the long/short case split and moment bridge, while the displayed statements (2.2)-(2.5) are not reliable enough for exact constants or powers.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on critical-line L-value, character-family, and integral-representation notation; all displayed ranges and exponents require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Huxley subdivision transfers the fixed-modulus estimate to the zeta case
accepted_units.why_material: For estimate (1.4), the paper specializes (1.2) to modulus one, applies Huxley's subdivision of the points, multiplies by the subdivision cost, and optimizes the auxiliary height parameter. This is a compact example of transferring an ensemble bound by partition and optimization.

accepted_units.why_material: The corollary proof restricts to zeros detected by a Dirichlet polynomial, raises the detecting inequality to a suitable integer power to create a polynomial in a chosen dyadic length range, applies the relevant large-value theorem, and optimizes the free length. The character-family variant changes which theorem estimate is invoked.
